If you use reddit's account deletion feature, your posts, comments, and other metadata are not removed from reddit's servers or public view. Only your username is publicly disassociated with them i.e. changed to read "[deleted]". reddit still retains all your info and the right to share and sell it.

The only way to make reddit get rid of your info is to overwrite (and then optionally delete) all your posts and comments, one by one. Overwriting alone gets rid of the info, because reddit currently does not version posts and comments. The January 1, 2016 Privacy Policy update will give them the right to do so.

Below, I am listing all the reddit user data scrubbing tools that I know of, separated into groups:

# **Backup**

If you want to back your comments up before you overwrite and/or delete them, the following tools may help.

Note that reddit limits comment access via user profile and API to both the 1000 most recent comments and the past 6 months. None of the below tools can access comments beyond those limits. There is no known workaround. A workaround has been figured out, see [this post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/759426).

* [Autopager](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/autopager-fixed/) - For Firefox. Implements infinite scrolling for many sites, including reddit. After installing and configuring the extension, scroll down in your comments page as far as it will go to get all your comments on one page, then save as HTML. * [Reddit Infinite Scrolling](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/reddit-infinite-scrolling/ngcdiindjnabamiehkinpjhkihgfanof?hl=en) - For Chrome. Implements infinite scrolling for reddit. After installing and configuring the extension, scroll down in your comments page as far as it will go to get all your comments on one page, then save as HTML. * [Shreddit](https://github.com/x89/Shreddit) - Python-based. Can back up or delete comments, make sure you choose the right option at the right time. * [Unnamed Python Script](http://hastebin.com/anatirewot.py) - Python-based. Also requires PRAW. Produces a JSON file.

# **Overwriting/Editing**

Tools in this group overwrite or edit your posts and comments with an exit message.

You may optionally use reddit's account deletion feature **after** running any one of these tools, so that your username is publicly disassociated with the overwritten posts and comments, as well.

Note that reddit limits comment access via user profile and API to both the 1000 most recent comments and the past 6 months. None of the below tools can access comments beyond those limits. There is no known workaround. A workaround has been figured out, see [this post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/759426).

* [Reddit Overwrite](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/10380-reddit-overwrite) - GreaseMonkey-based. Compatible with most mainstream browsers when a GreaseMonkey-compatible scripting extension is installed first. More details are available in [this Voat post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/241535). Overwrites all your posts and comments with a short, civil exit message telling people that you are done with reddit. **Not auto-censored by any subs.** * [Reddit Overwrite Extended](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/10905-reddit-overwrite-extended) - GreaseMonkey-based. Compatible with most mainstream browsers when a GreaseMonkey-compatible scripting extension is installed first. More details are available in [this Voat post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/241535). Overwrites all your posts and comments with an extended, opinionated exit message that expresses dissatisfaction with reddit management and announces that you are moving to Voat. **Auto-censored by several default and large subs.** * [Reddit Overwrite Extended With List of Alternatives](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/16006-reddit-overwrite-extended-with-list-of-alternatives) - GreaseMonkey-based. Compatible with most mainstream browsers when a GreaseMonkey-compatible scripting extension is installed first. More details are available in [this Voat post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/241535). Overwrites all your posts and comments with an extended, opinionated exit message that expresses dissatisfaction with reddit management and announces that you are moving to a reddit alternative. **Not auto-censored by any subs. RECOMMENDED.** * [Reddit Overwrite Extended Edit Only](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/10907-reddit-overwrite-extended-edit-only) - GreaseMonkey-based. Compatible with most mainstream browsers when a GreaseMonkey-compatible scripting extension is installed first. More details are available in [this Voat post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/241535). Prefixes all your posts and comments with an extended, opinionated exit message that expresses dissatisfaction with reddit management and announces that you are moving to Voat. **Auto-censored by several default and large subs.**

# **Complete Deletion**

All listed tools overwrite your posts and comments with null, inconsequential, or random data before deleting them.

You may optionally use reddit's account deletion feature **after** running any one of these tools, so that your username is publicly disassociated with the deleted posts and comments, as well.

Note that reddit limits comment access via user profile and API to both the 1000 most recent comments and the past 6 months. None of the below tools can access comments beyond those limits. There is no known workaround. A workaround has been figured out, see [this post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/759426).

* [Scrubber](http://scrubber.aiham.net/) - Web-based. * [RedWipe](https://github.com/crashcoredump/RedWipe), [RedWipe (forked, deleted)](https://github.com/guyintruck/RedWipe), [RedWipe (forked)](https://github.com/PuttItOut/RedWipe) - Windows-based. The last fork is the most advanced. * [RedEraser](https://github.com/THEMVFFINMAN/RedEraser) - Python-based. Also requires PRAW. * [Reddit Secure Delete](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/5550-reddit-secure-delete) - GreaseMonkey-based. Compatible with most mainstream browsers when a GreaseMonkey-compatible scripting extension is installed first. More details are available [in this Voat post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/241535). * [Shreddit](https://github.com/x89/Shreddit) - Python-based. Can back up or delete comments, make sure you choose the right option at the right time. * [reddit-eraser](https://github.com/chovy/reddit-eraser) - Node.js-based.

---

**Edit:** If you know of other tools that can help, mention them in the comments and I will edit them into this post.

**Edit 2:** If you've already deleted your reddit account, but less than 90 days ago, you may still be able to use one of these tools. [Contact reddit admins](https://www.reddit.com/contact/), ask them to reinstate the deleted account (tell them someone in your residence deleted it without your permission), and once your account has been reinstated, follow regular instructions. If it's been more than 90 days, they probably won't do it, but you can still try.

**Edit 3:** This is already stated in the linked "more details" post, but it bears repeating here, because people don't fucking read. There may be issues with recent versions of TamperMonkey, the version of GreaseMonkey for Google Chrome. The ideal platform for running GreaseMonkey scripts is GreaseMonkey on Mozilla Firefox with all extensions disabled, except possibly an infinite scrolling extension. Try that if possible.

**Edit 4:** The claim of a 6 month limit on one's access to one's own comments was based on apparently inaccurate reports. Testing has revealed that it is **not** in effect on one's access to one's own comments, but on contributing to threads only. This development has also been edited into the body of the post.

**Edit 5:** A workaround.for the 1000 comment limit has been figured out, see [this post](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/759426). This development has also been edited into the body of the post.

Daily Devotional - Happy Thanksgiving!

November 24

17 Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone. 18 Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works. (James 2:17-18 KJV)

Some people have thought that this verse contradicts the Grace teaching of Paul, but it doesn’t. What James is saying is that true faith will always have works of faith (not of the law) to go along with it, as if one says he has faith, yet doesn’t have any actions to prove it, then he is not telling the truth (James 2:20). If one truly has faith in what Jesus has done for us, then it will always cause them to have works of love, as that is the fruit of true bible faith. You can not have true faith in Jesus, without having any fruit (works of faith) to show for it. If you don’t have any visible signs of being born again, then you probably are not saved. Anyone that is truly saved can not help but want to live for Jesus, and show His love in their actions toward others. The greatest fruit of being truly saved is having love for your neighbor (other people), as Jesus taught (John 13:34-35).

Many people say they are Christians, and have saving faith in Jesus, but they do not have any fruit (works of faith) in their lives to prove it. If one has the works of faith, out of love for Jesus, and not works of the law (trying to earn from God), then the works of faith shows that he is truly saved. A person doesn’t need to proclaim it, as the fruit of his salvation will show that he is truly saved. The same works that one has can be of faith or of the law, and it is the condition of the heart that determines what kind of works it is. If you are trying to earn something from God by your works, then it is of the law. If you are doing works because of your love for Jesus, because of what He did for you, then it becomes works of faith, and shows that you have the born again Spirit in you. Do what works you do because you love the Lord and all your works will prove to be of faith, and you must obey Jesus to assure your eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9).

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
